summary: Evaluation of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry (3,995 valid CGM entries, 86.0% time in range, 5.1% time below range, 8.9% time above range) demonstrates generally stable glycemic control managed via an AAPS closed-loop system utilizing SMB, UAM, Dynamic ISF, and GLP-1 therapy support. Zero explicit carbohydrate entries are recorded, indicating the system operates primarily via unannounced loop dynamics, UAM microbolusing, and SMBs. Areas for refinement include mitigating overnight dipping and afternoon hyperglycemic excursions.

analysis_steps.findings: Data quality is high with 98.7% CGM coverage and robust device status/treatment telemetry. Treatment data shows insulin delivery and GLP-1 administration, but an absence of explicit carbohydrate entries.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid entries over 14 days, 10 gaps (largest 65.0 minutes), 6,214 device statuses, 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit carbohydrate treatment logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall time-in-range is solid at 86.0%, but time below range (5.1%) and specific hypoglycemia events reaching the low 40s mg/dL present a key safety constraint, alongside afternoon hyperglycemic peaks up to ~290 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7 mg/dL, CV 32.6%, 16 glucose extremes noted with lows down to 41 mg/dL and highs up to 293 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal logs prevents direct correlation of glycemic excursions with specific food intake.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates maintain glucose near target but show early-morning dipping (local hours 0-2 showing up to 18.5% below range). Afternoon hours exhibit upward glucose drift.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose averages show hour 0 at 93.3 mg/dL (11.4% < 70) and hour 1 at 90.6 mg/dL (18.5% < 70); afternoon hours 15-18 average 148-162 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Confounding effect of unlogged meals on afternoon glucose trends.

analysis_steps.findings: The profile utilizes a flat 24-hour ISF of 56 mg/dL/U and variable CR segments with a 10-hour DIA. Combined with Dynamic ISF (70%), effective ISF is potent, contributing to nighttime dipping.
analysis_steps.evidence: Single ISF segment of 56 mg/dL/U, variable CR segments (10.5 to 13.2 g/U), 10h DIA, therapy response windows showing varied correction responses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact carb amounts missing, limiting direct validation of CR segments.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and active. With `smb_always_enabled=true`, the loop aggressively manages unannounced glucose fluctuations.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS settings show `smb_enabled=true`, `uam_enabled=true`, `smb_always_enabled=true`, `smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true`, 3-min interval, 15-min max SMB basal minutes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal logs to assess UAM accuracy versus unannounced intake.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is active at 70%, tightening effective ISF and increasing microbolus potency during downward trends.
Meals are unlogged, relying entirely on UAM and SMB reactive microbolusing. This handles most intake well but can lag behind rapid afternoon spikes or over-correct.
analysis_steps.evidence: Treatment summary shows 0 carb entries and 0 total carbs recorded across 14 days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of recorded meal carbohydrate entries.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carbs or extended boluses are utilized. Absorption modeling relies on default UAM impact and a 7-hour max absorption setting.
analysis_steps.evidence: No e-carb treatments present; AAPS meal max absorption hours set to 7 h, min 5m carb impact set to 8 mg/dL/5 min.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of declared meal composition or extended carb usage.

analysis_steps.findings: Data indicates solid overall time in range but highlights hypoglycemia risk (5.1% TBR) during overnight hours and unannounced afternoon hyperglycemia. Recommendations prioritize maintaining stable settings while initiating manual carb logging for validation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined evidence from CGM coverage, time-in-range metrics, hourly glucose distributions, and closed-loop telemetry.

strengths: High CGM data coverage (98.7%) with robust telemetry and device status recording.
Strong overall time in range (86.0%) over the 14-day evaluation period.
Effective automated closed-loop management utilizing SMB, UAM, and Dynamic ISF to maintain stability.
issues: Elevated time below range (5.1%) with specific overnight dipping (up to 18.5% below range in local hours 0-2).
Afternoon and evening hyperglycemic excursions (local hours 15-18 averaging up to 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1% time above range).
Complete absence of recorded meal carbohydrate entries, forcing reliance on reactive UAM/SMB delivery.

recommendations.title: Initiate Carbohydrate Logging
recommendations.description: Log explicit carbohydrate amounts for meals over a 3-5 day period to evaluate actual postprandial response curves and validate current carb ratios.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings unchanged while establishing consistent manual carbohydrate logging to evaluate postprandial dynamics.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall time in range is strong (86.0%) and current glycemic patterns are adequately managed by the automated loop. Nighttime dipping and afternoon peaks are appropriately monitored via existing safety limits and dynamic sensitivity.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose trends and daytime excursions over the next 7 days after introducing explicit meal logging.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: With zero explicitly recorded carb treatment entries in the dataset and frequent reliance on UAM and SMB (`smb_always_enabled=true`), the system operates primarily in an unannounced/hybrid loop mode where postprandial rises and unlogged intake are managed reactively via UAM/SMB microbolusing and GLP-1 therapy support. Hypoglycemia risk (5.1% TBR) indicates that reactive microbolusing can occasionally over-deliver when combined with an effective ISF tightened by Dynamic ISF (70%).
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Introduce consistent manual carbohydrate logging for meals alongside prebolusing when possible to enable precise evaluation of carb ratios (CR) and allow the closed-loop system to utilize COB-driven dosing rather than relying solely on UAM/SMB reactive correction.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon/Evening Hyperglycemic Peaks (local hours 15-18 averages up to 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1% TAR)
exceptions.suggestion: Ensure pre-meal bolusing or explicit carb entry occurs prior to afternoon meals to prevent delayed UAM/SMB reaction curves from lagging behind rapid postprandial glucose rises.
exceptions.rationale: Data shows significant afternoon glucose excursions that eventually require aggressive correction boluses or high temporary basal rates, pointing to unannounced or late-absorbed intake.

exceptions.pattern: Overnight and Early Morning Dips (local hours 0-2 showing up to 18.5% time below range)
exceptions.suggestion: Avoid late-evening unannounced corrections or heavy snacking without bolus entry, as lingering SMB activity from evening meal recovery can drive overnight dipping.
exceptions.rationale: Late evening/nighttime telemetry reveals active IOB and dynamic sensitivity adjustments driving glucose down toward or below 70 mg/dL during early sleep hours.

meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Logging explicit carbohydrate amounts for meals over a 3-5 day period to evaluate actual postprandial response curves and validate current CR settings.

implementation_steps: Verify current AAPS profile settings and sensor telemetry against closed-loop performance.
Begin recording explicit meal carbohydrate entries for all meals to establish a reliable baseline for carb ratio evaluation.
Monitor overnight glucose trends and afternoon excursions over a 7-day observation period before considering any parameter adjustments.
Review glycemic metrics and time-in-range following the introduction of manual carb logging.
education: Closed-loop systems with SMB enabled (`smb_always_enabled=true`) rely heavily on accurate carbohydrate and meal announcements to optimize insulin delivery and minimize postprandial spikes.

Dynamic ISF adjusts effective insulin sensitivity in real-time based on short-term glucose movement, which can enhance correction potency but requires careful observation to avoid hypoglycemia during downward trends.
GLP-1 therapy can slow gastric emptying, shifting carbohydrate absorption curves and requiring appropriate alignment with meal bolus timing and maximum absorption settings.
